title: Performance of Panchasamskaram
body:
Performance of Panchasamskaram

By resorting to an Acharya and gaining his acceptance, the person will soon realize, by the grace of the Acharya, true knowledge, non-attachment to worldly pleasures, and devotion to the Lord starts to bloom like a flower.  In Srivaishnava Sampradayam, the panchasamskaram is the most crucial ceremony performed by the Acharya. The Acharya, out of compassion, without any expectations, accepts the disciple regardless of their caste or creed. The Acharya then performs panchasamskaram, and then the disciple becomes a Sri Vaishnava. Being a Sri Vaishnava is not determined by birth. This is the reason why one can see men and women from all communities and all walks of life as a Srivaishnava. 
The panchasamskaram, as the name suggests, consists of five samskarams, namely,

i) Tapa Samaskaram: The Acharya embosses the impressions of the Panchajanya Shankam and the Sudharshana Chakram on the left and right arms of the disciple.

ii) Pundra Samskaram: The Acharya makes the disciple aware of the places in the body where the upavyuha forms of the Lord Sriman Narayana are to be worshipped. Each upavyuha-sthanam is represented by one of the twelve thiruman-kapu adorned by the disciple. The tiruman represents the Lord, whereas the Sricharnam represents Mahalakshmi. The worship of the Lord is performed by holding the hands in Anjali-mudra and reciting “Keshavaya Namaha” prefixed by the Pranava. Similarly, Devi Mahalakshmi is worshipped, reciting “Sriyai Namaha” prefixed by the Pranava. 

iii) Nama Samskaram: The Acharya adds the suffix of dasan to the disciple's name, indicating the disciple is now an eternal servant to the Lord and Swami Ramanujar.

iv) Mantra Samskaram: Of all the five samskarams performed, this is the most important without an iota of doubt. The mantras received when this samskaram is being delivered are together known as the Rahasya Trayam or the three divine secrets.

v)Yagna Samskaram: The Acharya teaches the disciple the ways of Bhagavadh Aaradhana and the methods to perform Salagrama pooja.
